fields.meta_description: Build an expense request form that checks the budget code and gets an approver's yes before anyone spends money. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Expense Request Form That Clears Spending in Advance
fields.hero_description: Describe your spending rules and who approves what. Emergent builds the expense request form, checks each estimate against its budget code and routes it before any money goes out.
fields.features_heading: What Gets Checked Before Anyone Signs
fields.features_subheading: A printed request asks for an amount and a signature. Each piece below answers a question finance would otherwise chase over email.
fields.feature_1:
Estimates that total themselves

Add a line for each cost, such as seats, labor or delivery, with a quantity and unit price. The form multiplies and adds the lines, and the approver reads one total with its math.
fields.feature_2:
A budget code on every request

Require a budget or cost center code before submit. The form looks up what that code has left and shows the approver the balance after this request, beside the amount asked for.
fields.feature_3:
Approvers matched to the amount

Send small requests to a department head and add finance or the CFO above a limit you set. Each decision is saved on the request with the approver's name and the exact time.
fields.feature_4:
Quotes and reasons required

Ask for a written business reason on every request and a vendor quote above an amount you choose. A request missing either one stays in draft and never reaches an approver half done.
fields.feature_5:
Approval numbers that follow the spend

Give each approved request a number like ER-1042 and send it to the requester by email or Slack. The receipt filed later cites it and sits beside the approval it was spent against.
fields.feature_6:
The whole app, exported

Export the full codebase to your GitHub on paid plans when finance wants the app on its own servers. The requests table moves along too, with every decision and its comment intact.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Requests Filed Before the Money Moves
fields.tab_content_1:
A monthly seat price turned into a yearly one

Software at Fernbrook Analytics is bought by the seat and billed monthly, which hides what a tool costs over a year. The marketing lead asks for 6 seats of a scheduling tool at $24 a seat. Her department head sees $1,728 for the year, plus her answer on whether the plan renews on its own, before he approves.
fields.tab_content_2:
A $6,400 repair held for its second quote

Dock doors at Globex Cold Storage take a beating from forklifts. Policy there asks for two vendor quotes on anything over $5,000. The facilities manager files a $6,400 door repair with one quote attached, and the form keeps it in draft until another arrives. The operations director then compares both quotes on one screen.
fields.tab_content_3:
When the club account runs short by $120

Club money at Cedar Ridge High sits in small accounts that run dry by spring. The robotics advisor asks for $420 of motors and sensors against the club account, which has $300 left. The form shows the gap and asks for another code. She charges the rest to the booster grant, and the principal approves the split.
fields.tab_content_4:
Lunch for 40 approved before the caterer is booked

Once a quarter, Harborview Dental closes early for a team lunch. The office manager requests catering for 40 at $18 a head. The owner approves the $720 from a Slack message, and the request becomes ER-1042. When the caterer's receipt comes in, it cites that number and lands beside the approval.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Expense Request Form
fields.howto_description: Most of the work happens before the prompt. Agree on what needs approval in advance and where each signer's limit sits, and the form follows from those answers.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick the fields an approver reads
fields.howto_step_1_des: Find out which purchases need a yes before anyone spends, and at what amount. Many teams let small buys go on a company card and ask for requests above a set figure. If nobody has written that figure down, agree on it with finance now.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List what an approver needs to decide: the item and vendor, an estimate broken into lines, the budget code and a short business reason. Leave out anything finance never reads. Each extra field slows the requester and changes no decision.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Map each amount band to an approver by role, such as a department head up to a limit and finance above it. Roles outlast staff changes. Name a backup for each role, because requests stall whenever the one person who signs is out.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the fields, the approval limits and any quote rule into one plain-English prompt. Emergent builds the expense request form with routing between approvers and a requests table behind it. Change a limit later by asking for the new one.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Point the app at wherever budgets live, whether that is a spreadsheet or your accounting software. Approvers then see what a code has left before deciding, and a request that would overdraw its code asks the requester for another one.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide how approved requests are numbered, and ask people to write that number on the invoice or receipt. Matching a claim to its approval afterward then takes one search in the requests table instead of a hunt through old email threads.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 File a test request over the limit
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before rollout, submit a test above your top approval limit with a quote missing. Check that it stays in draft until the quote is added, reaches each approver in order and lands in the table with every decision and its time.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is Jotform and Typeform templates, a New Orleans expense approval request PDF, a St. John's reimbursement form, a SurveyMonkey reimbursement template, Template.net, a Droplet form and a Pinterest board. Most of them blur asking before spending with claiming afterward, and every one ends at a signature line. This page is the request filed before any money moves: an estimate, a budget code, a written reason and the right approver, then an approval number that the receipt cites later. Four non-travel cases show it: a software subscription priced for the year, a repair that needs a second quote, a school club order split across two codes and a team lunch approved before the caterer is booked. Receipts filed afterward stay on the expense report sibling; trips stay on the travel request sibling.
